LutCam Spektrafilm integration

Upstream Android engine: https://github.com/thetechgeekko/Spektrafilm-android
Commit: 15fb120996f03fc1e58a9a9d819e335f65d7a092
Film modeling powered by spektrafilm (Andrea Volpato):
https://github.com/andreavolpato/spektrafilm

Engine C++ sources (including embedded Vulkan shaders) and 28 material profiles
were copied unchanged. UPSTREAM_SHA256.json records the copied source hashes.
The outer CMakeLists.txt integrates a static engine with LutCam's own JNI bridge;
the upstream editor JNI, tests, codecs, ICC files, optional Highway/TBB dependencies
and the upstream editor application are not used. The original NOTICE.md and
LICENSE are retained verbatim; references there to omitted components describe
the upstream application, not additional libraries linked into LutCam.

LutCam additions: camera display-RGB decoding/colour adaptation, fixed film/print
pairings, offline LUT preview, and full-resolution RAW photo export. The native
pinned engine files remain unchanged on disk. The executable is locally modified
by the checked build overlays in third_party/spektrafilm_android/patches/.
CMake requires Python 3 (standard library only), verifies the original hashes and
shader checksums, then generates the six modified translation units in the build
directory. The source distribution includes overlays, GLSL, embedded SPIR-V and
the shader generator. Preview assets are derived with the upstream
spk_bake_cube_lut API, shaper=1, and converted from blue-fast to red-fast PLUT v1.
Each of 20 looks has a 65^3 RGB16 LUT. The camera OES shader decodes its SDR
transfer/primaries, converts to linear ProPhoto D50, then applies the sRGB OETF
per channel as the LUT's input shaper. Output is encoded sRGB. OES sampling has
already expanded YUV range. Preview needs no CPU frame readback or full model.

The bake keeps the pointwise spectral/density/print/scan transform; grain,
halation/scatter, DIR spatial diffusion, glare and scanner unsharp are excluded
by the upstream API. Camera AE has already acted, so no model AE is baked in.
The manifest and SHA256SUMS.json record pairing, engine commit, checksums and
4096 off-grid samples per look. Normalized encoded-RGB interpolation RMSE ranges
0.00131-0.00249, with worst individual channel errors up to 0.0752 over the full
ProPhoto input cube. This is a preview approximation, not a full-effect render.

Photos develop the full captured RAW using black/LSC correction, demosaic,
white balance, camera CCM and Bradford adaptation to linear ProPhoto D50.
An explicitly owned native float32 RGB buffer preserves HDR values above 1 and is borrowed by the serialized film worker under its owner lock. The product capture path moves the ISP vector, runs the same full model, fills an RGBA_8888 Bitmap directly and closes the input owner on success or exception. It does not write/read LCRF or RGB8 intermediates. Debug capture may additionally save LCRF; LCRF v1 remains the diagnostic replay format. No prior ISP display
tone curve, classic LUT, gamma or 8-bit intermediate is applied. The full native
simulation entry is used with gpu_export enabled, one model auto-exposure
normalization, all default grain, halation/scatter, DIR diffusion, printing and
glare retained. Optional creative filters retain upstream defaults (off).
LutCam then quantizes directly into Bitmap pixels and rotates/crops/encodes the JPEG. LUT preview continues during
saving. Original preview-snapshot photo export has been removed.

The full photo graph is CPU/Vulkan hybrid, with upstream per-stage self-checks
and CPU fallback, not an entirely GPU-resident pipeline. DIR diffusion precludes
the upstream resident pointwise chain but independent GPU stages still engage.
GPU grain/glare samplers may produce a different stochastic realization. No
spatial stage or photo resolution is reduced to qualify for a GPU path.

Earlier baseline HONOR BKQ_AN10 qualification: all 20 1920x1440 live LUT previews ran around 30 fps.
The camera-frame/window-submission cadence is a short-window throughput measure,
not panel presentation time or sensor-to-screen latency. A 512x384 HDR fixture
with stochastic grain/glare disabled gave CPU/Vulkan RGB RMSE 1.89e-7 and maximum
4.31e-6; it does not establish pixel identity for stochastic full photos.
A Portra 800 RAW 4096x3072 produced a portrait 3072x4096 JPEG, 36 Vulkan submissions,
7317ms model wall time and 7691ms native/file-I/O call time after qualification
warmup. Earlier CPU processing took 10781ms on a different frame, so this is not
a strict same-RAW A/B or total shutter-to-gallery benchmark. Display preview and
RAW photo exposure/tone still need reference calibration. Other devices,
orientations, front camera and sustained thermal behaviour are unqualified.

Earlier memory-handoff benchmark (same device, same saved 4096x3072 RAW development,
same full Portra 800 GPU-export parameters): the ISP file and memory float32
planes matched bit-for-bit. After warmup, four measured runs per route in
ABBA/BAAB order gave median 4824ms legacy file transport versus 4335ms native
memory-to-Bitmap, a 10.1% reduction. All rendered RGB8 pixels matched exactly;
the source hash remained unchanged, double-close was harmless, and a closed
owner rejected rendering. Timings start from a shared resident RAW-linear plane
and end at Bitmap; RAW development, initialization, rotation/crop, JPEG and gallery
are excluded. The common input remains resident for repeated legacy comparisons.
Temperature/background load were not controlled; this is not a shutter latency
or cross-device guarantee. Native diagnostics now expose transport/packing and
internal grain phases, GPU grain engagement/refusal and GPU FFT counts. The
fixture's grain sampler engaged the GPU; intermediate layer/blur traffic remains
an optimization opportunity. Actual live memory-capture qualification is recorded
separately in the accompanying validation report.

Earlier live memory-capture regression passed all 20 LUT selections and classic/none.
One 4096x3072 RAW -> 3072x4096 portrait JPEG took 5652ms from test shutter to
observed saved result: RAW capture/development 623ms, full film-to-Bitmap 4491ms,
RAW-to-Bitmap 5114ms, with JPEG/gallery afterwards. Engine initialization had
already been warmed by the CPU/GPU qualification fixture. The full film graph
made 36 Vulkan submissions; default spatial/stochastic effects were retained.
Distinct OES timestamps and successful window submissions continued during film
processing (23.9fps over one 2-second window); median of the 20 look-selection
windows was 30.2fps. These are single-device short-window observations, not a
stable shutter-latency, panel timing or sustained-performance guarantee.

2026-10-22 local scan-tail optimization: the common default encoded-sRGB scanner
exit combines additive glare, reflected separable FIR, unsharp mixing, the existing
CAT02 round-trip matrix and encoding/clipping in two dispatches and one submission.
This removes the full-size f64 scan plane and unsharp copy. Spectral scan still
returns f32 to the host before the tail upload; this is not full GPU residency.
The overlay also corrects buffer-before-bound-memory destruction order. Existing
model effects and resolution are retained. Unsupported custom settings, storage
limits, allocation failures or on-device reference-check failures retain the
previous tail. See patches/README.md for the exact eligibility and shader rebuild.

Same-device, same 4096x3072 RAW-linear Portra 800 full-model comparison, native
memory transport for both routes, four measured runs each after warmup in ABBA/
BAAB order: median to-Bitmap 5504ms -> 4904ms (10.9% reduction), scan 1099ms ->
522ms (52.5%), scan_spatial 780ms -> 297ms. Full-model submissions 36 -> 30.
All 20 complete-model profile comparisons engaged the new tail; maximum float
error 4.83e-7, full-RAW RGB8 maximum difference 1. Unsupported/nonfinite inputs
were rejected without overwriting output. The f32 tail is tolerance bounded,
not byte-identical to the previous f64 spatial operations. These timings exclude
RAW development, initialization, rotation/crop, JPEG/gallery; temperature and
background load were not controlled. No cross-device or sustained guarantee.
This benchmark supersedes prior historical measurements for the scanner change;
do not compare unrelated historical inputs as a strict performance A/B.

Current live regression passed all 20 previews and classic/none. The optimized
tail engaged, 4096x3072 RAW saved as 3072x4096 JPEG, with 30 full-model Vulkan
submissions. Observed shutter-to-JPEG was 8754ms: RAW capture/development 1235ms,
film-to-Bitmap 6652ms; preview continued at 29.9fps in one processing window.
This different live input/load is not the controlled A/B and shows real latency
still varies. The scene had no reliable orientation/detail reference: visual
inspection confirms portrait proportions/no obvious stripes, not orientation
calibration or fine-detail quality. Engine was warmed by qualification.

2026-10-22 second performance pass: resident grain layers, finite-or-zero layer
sanitization, the original particle shader, density_min subtraction and final
reflected FIR run in five dispatches/one submission. Original layer and particle
SPIR-V, RNG, seeds, cell derivation, dye-cloud taps and normal-branch policy are
unchanged. Stock tables carry missing values; sanitization matches the previous
host upload. The nine-channel device scratch is reused for the vertical FIR
with read-to-write ordering after sampling. At 4096x3072 this removes the 432MiB
host layer allocation and 864MiB layer readback-plus-upload; 432MiB device scratch
is still required. The scan tail also parallelizes finite checks/staging copies,
without changing arithmetic. Unsupported micro-structure/wide kernels, explicit
SPK_GPU_BLUR=0, device limits or self-check failure retain the old complete path.

The first-use real-profile check compares old GPU stages and branch counts with
the resident chain. All 20 full-model fixtures engage, max float error 8.22e-6,
RGB8 max 1; full-resolution same-RAW RGB8 max also 1. Invalid/unsupported requests
leave caller output unchanged. This is not CPU/GPU stochastic pixel identity.
Same fixed 4096x3072 RAW, four measured runs each after warmup, ABBA/BAAB, first
scan-tail shader active on both routes: median to-Bitmap 4092ms -> 3649ms (10.8%),
grain 486ms -> 130ms (73.2%), scan 349ms -> 275ms (21.4%). Scan upload 70 -> 28ms,
readback/check/copy 61 -> 29ms. Timing excludes RAW development, initialization,
rotation/crop, JPEG/gallery. Different sessions have different load/temperature;
compare this interleaved A/B only, not earlier historical absolute timings.
The original particle shader's omitted submission counter is corrected in the
generated overlay; historical submission counts are not directly comparable.
Full effects and photo dimensions remain unchanged. See patches/README.md and
the accompanying validation report for scope, shaders and exact measurements.

Final second-pass live regression passed all 20 LUT selections and classic/none,
plus one real Portra 800 capture: RAW 4096x3072 -> JPEG 3072x4096. Resident grain
and parallel scan transfer both engaged. Observed shutter-to-JPEG 5153ms, RAW
capture/development 643ms, film-to-Bitmap 4019ms, RAW-to-Bitmap 4662ms. Processing
preview window 23.4fps, median selection window 30.2fps (throughput, not panel
latency). The output was inspected for orientation/proportion/obvious stripes;
no calibrated colour/detail target was present. Engine warmed by qualification.
This different live frame is not a stable latency or cross-scene speed guarantee.

2026-10-22 third performance pass: the GPU print integral's CPU tail evaluates
the two existing clamp/floor seams directly in f64, avoiding a full 288MiB f64
plane and redundant log10/pow10 work at 4096x3072. Midgray, preflash, exposure and
B/W corrections remain; active enlarger optical diffusion keeps the old route.
DIR retains f64 curve construction/matrix/interpolation, but its correction and
diffused host planes are f32 at the SAME conversion seams used by the existing
GPU path. This removes 288MiB of host scratch at that stage. These savings are
per-stage, not a combined process-peak claim. The CPU oracle is unchanged.

A local spatial shader assigns independent (column,channel) IIR lanes instead of
sequential channels in a thread. Original double-float/Dekker arithmetic, f64
coefficients, FIR, boundaries and blending remain. A first-use paired comparison
checks mixed FIR/IIR on odd geometry and sigma 3/12/63/256 before enabling it;
failure or unsupported additional dispatch range retains the original pipeline.
Source notices, GLSL, SPIR-V, generator and checksums are included. An experimental
native FMA residual failed the device primitive check and is not shipped.
All default effects/full photo resolution remain; this is still CPU/Vulkan hybrid.

Third-pass final fixed-RAW A/B: both routes keep the prior two optimizations,
only the three new changes are toggled. Same HONOR 4096x3072 RAW-linear plane,
one warmup per route, four measured each in ABBA/BAAB: to-Bitmap median 4242 ->
3125ms (26.3%); halation 851 -> 600ms, DIR 919 -> 549ms, print 686 -> 289ms.
All 20 full-model fixtures had zero float/RGB8 difference; full-resolution RAW
RGB8 max difference was also zero. This is measured agreement for these inputs,
not universal floating-point bit identity. Excludes RAW development, initialization,
rotation, JPEG/gallery. Temperature/background load were not controlled; do not
calculate cumulative gains from historical sessions' absolute times.

Third-pass live regression passed 20 previews and classic/none, plus one Portra
800 RAW 4096x3072 -> 3072x4096 JPEG. All three new stages engaged. Observed first
shutter-to-JPEG 7643ms, RAW capture/development 1290ms, film-to-Bitmap 5525ms;
processing preview window 29.5fps, selection median 30.2fps. Portrait proportions,
orientation and obvious stripes were inspected, without a calibration target.
First full-frame preparation, scene and device load differ from the warmed A/B;
the extra repeated-shot test stopped when the phone switched to another app.
No stable repeated-shot latency result is claimed. Engine warmed by qualification.

Engine GPLv3 and profile licenses/notices are bundled under assets/legal/spektrafilm
and shown in the Film tab. The source snapshot accompanying the debug APK contains
the Android build sources, integration, profiles and license material.


2026-10-22 fourth performance pass: the scanner borrows completed resident grain
buffers, with separate device input, mapped output and scratch, explicit transfer
usage/barriers and the same fence/mutex. At 4096x3072 this avoids growing three
additional 144MiB scan buffers (432MiB capacity, not an OS RSS measurement). The
glare buffer remains private. Unsupported/nonresident cases retain old storage.
Shaders and scan arithmetic are unchanged. AE preview sampling now caches integer
reflected tap indices and distributes independent pixels among workers, retaining
all original f64 per-pixel sums, coefficients, sample coordinates and AE policy.
The original small preview, full-resolution photo and all effects remain.

Same fixed RAW, full Portra 800, previous three passes active on both routes:
eight fresh processes in ABBA/BAAB order, first full-size render and immediate
warm repeat each. Model-to-Bitmap median 3157 -> 2894ms cold (8.3%), 2566 -> 2325ms
warm (9.4%). All 16 RGB8 hashes matched; all 20 smaller complete-model fixtures
had zero float/RGB8 error. Host 1/4-worker AE tests also retained EV/sample bits.
Observed agreement is not universal floating-point identity. Excludes engine
creation, fixture loading, RAW development, rotation/JPEG/gallery. Background
activity and temperature were not controlled; these are single-device results.
Save diagnostics separately time transform, JPEG, gallery and thumbnail phases.
The accompanying performance-v4 APK uses com.example.rawsoftwareisp.performance,
label LutCam 性能版, for parallel installation; the default source build ID is
unchanged, so pass the documented Gradle properties to reproduce this package.

Fourth-pass live regression passed all 20 previews and classic/none, full Portra
800, RAW 4096x3072 -> JPEG 3072x4096. New stages engaged. Observed first shutter
to saved result 5440ms: RAW capture/development 1169ms, film-to-Bitmap 3565ms,
transform 305ms, JPEG 228ms, gallery 87ms, thumbnail 8ms. Processing preview window
24.4fps (camera/window throughput, not display latency). Portrait proportions,
orientation and obvious stripes inspected; no calibrated detail/colour target.
Engine warmed with small qualification fixtures; first full-size live capture.
This separate scene/load is not a historical shutter-latency A/B or stable bound.


2026-10-22 fifth performance pass: partial resident expose -> complete halation/
scatter -> exposure-log chain, using original shader bytes and f32 seams. One
GPU mutex covers the sequence, descriptor front changes and memory barriers.
Only successful finite readback publishes caller pixels; every exit closes the
resident frame. A first-use small old/new comparison gates the optimization.
Unsupported creative settings keep the complete original route. Two 288MiB host
f64 transient planes are avoided at 12MP; new resident buffers/staging also use
capacity, so this is not a net process-peak/RSS claim. The whole graph remains
CPU/Vulkan hybrid, with all effects and full resolution.

Final RGB8 packing now uses parallel disjoint 32x32 tiles, fusing the existing
post-film digital crop and integer orientation into the same pass. Quantization,
alpha, crop dimensions and JPEG quality remain unchanged. It avoids the separate
Java rotation and extra Bitmap. Classic output is unchanged. Host tests cover
all four angles with independently enumerated cropped pixel labels, row padding,
invalid crop and parallel packing versus the original quantization.

Same fixed RAW, previous four passes active on both sides, eight fresh processes
in ABBA/BAAB order, first full-size render + warm repeat each. End at equivalent
3072x4096 portrait Bitmap: baseline includes original Java rotation, new route
packs directly. First-render median 3478 -> 3138ms (9.8%); warm 2536 -> 2023ms
(20.2%). Warm model invocation 2206 -> 1976ms, native output 75 -> 31ms. All 16
RGB8 hashes matched; all 20 complete-model fixtures had zero float/RGB8 error.
Failure output preservation, recovery, f64 input/alias checks pass. Excludes engine
initialization, fixture loading, RAW development and JPEG/gallery. Temperature
and background activity uncontrolled; observed agreement is not universal float
identity. A smaller IIR workgroup experiment had no stable extra gain and is not
shipped. The full engine's spatial filters remain a main bottleneck.

Live regression: all 20 previews and classic/none passed. RAW 4096x3072 -> JPEG
3072x4096; partial residency and fused output engaged. Observed first shutter to
saved result 3937ms, RAW capture/development 668ms, film-to-oriented-Bitmap 2868ms,
JPEG 176ms, gallery 84ms, thumbnail 10ms. Processing preview window 21.2fps,
selection median 30.2fps (throughput, not display latency). Portrait orientation,
proportions and obvious stripes inspected without a colour/detail target. Engine
warmed with small qualification fixtures, first full-size live capture. Separate
scene/load; not a historical shutter-latency A/B or sustained guarantee.


2026-10-22 sixth performance pass: mapped DIR transport reuses the already-ready
resident frame pair/staging. The original f64 CPU silver/matrix correction writes
straight into mapped input; the original complete diffusion executes, and the
original f64 interpolation consumes mapped readback directly. Shader bytes, RNG,
coefficients, interpolation and f32 conversion seams are unchanged. Two private
144MiB f32 host vectors, their initialization and copies are avoided at 12MP
(288MiB transient capacity, not an OS RSS measurement). No additional full-size
buffer growth on this route; missing capacity keeps the previous complete path.

GPU mutex/fences cover CPU callbacks and device work. Finite success is required
before finish; every exit closes residency. CPU callback exceptions propagate to
the renderer, never retry on partially written aliased output. Resident readback
orders both transfer and shader writes. A first-use exact old/new transport check
covers odd geometry, mixed FIR/IIR and sigma .65/3/12/63/256. Explicit tests cover
nonfinite fill, GPU sigma refusal after upload, prepare/finish cancellation,
frame closure and recovery against original diffusion. All 20 complete profiles
had zero float/RGB8 difference; this remains observed-input agreement rather than
a universal numeric or CPU/GPU stochastic identity claim.

Same fixed 4096x3072 RAW-linear plane, all five previous passes on both sides,
eight fresh processes ABBA/BAAB, first full-size and warm repeat each, equivalent
3072x4096 portrait Bitmap: median cold 3141 -> 3027ms (3.6%), warm 2058 -> 1927ms
(6.4%); warm DIR 463 -> 340ms (26.6%). All 16 RGB8 hashes matched. Excludes engine
initialization, fixture loading, RAW development, JPEG/gallery. Temperature and
background load uncontrolled. Existing preview/full-model effects/resolution and
parallel package ID are retained; the whole graph is still CPU/Vulkan hybrid.
Sixth-pass live regression passed all 20 lightweight previews and classic/none.
Full Portra 800 RAW 4096x3072 -> JPEG 3072x4096, mapped DIR engaged, self-check
error zero. Observed first shutter-to-saved result 4333ms: RAW capture/development
664ms, film-to-oriented-Bitmap 3291ms, JPEG 160ms, gallery 77ms, thumbnail 9ms.
Mapped DIR prepare/upload/diffusion/readback/finish: 16/8/269/18/31ms. Processing

2026-10-22 seventh performance pass: transpose-only shared-memory padding from
32x32 to a 32x33 row layout. Pixel indices/operations, original IIR/FIR math,
coefficients, reflected boundaries, RNG and model settings remain unchanged.
Only op 17 uses the additional pipeline; original complete route is retained.
Process-once exact old/new diffusion qualification covers narrow/single axes,
partial edge tiles, mixed FIR/IIR and sigma .65/2.999/12/256 before residency.
GLSL/SPIR-V hashes and a fourth local shader generator are included.

Two separate balanced eight-process ABBA/BAAB blocks, same 4096x3072 RAW-linear
fixture, all six previous optimizations on both sides. Each process renders a
first full-size portrait Bitmap then a warm repeat. All 32 RGB8 hashes matched;
all 20 complete stock fixtures had zero float/RGB8 difference. Host integration
and metering tests passed. Invalid/refusal/cancellation/recovery checks retained.
First block warm 1816 -> 1756ms (3.3%); second 1704 -> 1699ms (0.3%). Pooled warm
median 1771 -> 1738ms (1.9%); pooled GPU halation 344 -> 330ms and DIR 224 ->210ms.
Pooled cold median 2728 -> 2785ms (2.1% slower), including new first-use checks.
This is a small, variable warm gain, not a first-photo speedup or stable bound.
No trials excluded. Temperature/background load uncontrolled on a single device.
Excludes engine initialization, fixture loading, RAW development and JPEG/gallery.
A shared FIR coefficient experiment showed less than 0.3% gain and is not shipped.
